title: Activation Stewardship: Chefbook Sprint Notes
content:
Context and purpose:

Quick sprint notes from the cross-team chefbook session — trying to capture a pragmatic, small-footprint stewardship model for staged activations (canary / A/B) that product, SRE, and solutions eng can use without heavyweight ceremonies. Goal: remove ambiguity about who drives exposure decisions and what signals must be satisfied before moving from one slice to the next.

Why this doc exists (pain we saw):
- Repeated friction during multiwave rollouts: product wants to expand, SRE is nervous about CPU/latency, solutions eng worried about data regressions for tiered customers.
- No clear single owner for the "observe & greenlight" step, so changes sit in limbo.
- Existing playbooks are long and academic; we need a short-ceremony, role-first checklist that scales across 2-3 person teams.

High-level proposal (one-liner):
Create a small "Activation Chef" pattern: one designated steward per activation (product or PME) + two signal owners (SRE for infra + ML owner for quality). Steward is accountable for timing, comms, and the final go/no-go.

Roles and responsibilities (working):
- Activation Chef (steward): coordinates the waves, writes the exposure note, calls the activation slot. Typical: PM/PME or release owner.
- Infra Signal Owner (SRE): confirms telemetry (latency P50/P95, outage budget, queueing, infra autoscaler behavior).
- Model Quality Owner (ML/Product): confirms quality signals (regression guardrails, eval set A/B deltas, hallucination/error rate).
- Customer Success & Solutions Eng: invited to first two waves for high-risk customers; optional thereafter.
- Oncall/Incident Commander: ready to run rollback steps if thresholds breach.

Signal definitions (minimal actionable set):
- Latency: P95 end-to-end latency not > 2x baseline AND no sustained rising trend over 30m. (owner: SRE)
- Errors: 5xx or gateway failures < 0.05% sustained for 15m. (owner: SRE)
- Cost/Throughput anomaly: tokens-per-second or GPU utiliz > baseline + 30% for 15m (owner: SRE)
- Quality regression: primary metric delta (e.g., rerank NDCG or classification F1) < -1.5% vs control on core eval set AND no customer-impacting bias signals. (owner: Model Quality)
- Safety regressions: any flagged safety failure in canary slice -> immediate rollback. (owner: Model Quality / Safety)

Note: signal thresholds are intentionally conservative initially; steward can tighten/loosen with SRE/model owner agreement.

Activation cadence (practical, 3-wave pattern):
- Wave 0 (internal smoke): 0.1% internal traffic or synthetic traffic. Verify basic correctness and no crashes. Duration: 30m.
- Wave 1 (safety-sliced canary): 1% of traffic, heavily instrumented, include low-latency cohorts. Duration: 2h (minimum).
- Wave 2 (fast ramp): 10% of traffic, watch for long-tail regressions, run two A/B variants if applicable. Duration: 6h.
- Full (open): increase to 100% with staged autoscale and monitoring.

Decision checklist for steward before moving waves (short):
- Have infra and model owners validated the signals? (yes/no)
- Are there unresolved customer tickets that could be impacted? (list)
- Do we have a rollback patch and communication plan? (link)
- Have we reserved an activation slot in calendar + oncall coverage? (yes/no)
- Smoke test pass in staging and Wave 0 artifacts collected? (yes/no)

Rollback matrix (quick):
- Severity A: Safety violation or data leak => rollback immediately to last tagged model, page SEC/Safety and CS, open postmortem.
- Severity B: Model quality drops > 3% on critical eval or multiple CS reports for high-value customers => pause rollout, partial rollback for affected cohorts.
- Severity C: Infra degradation (P95 > 2x for > 30m or 5xx spike) => throttle and/or rollback dependent on SRE assessment.

Observability checklist (must-have dashboards / alerts):
- Live traffic slice view: per-slice latency + 5xx rate + tokens/sec (owner: SRE)
- Model quality stream: rolling eval metric delta vs control, safety flag counts (owner: ML)
- User-facing error funnel: session drop rate, feature-specific failure rates (owner: product analytics)
- Incident playbook link and rollback runnable script: (owner: steward / release eng)

Experiment / A/B considerations (when both are used):
- If we run A/B in Wave 2, limit sample size per variant such that statistical power > 80% for primary metric. Do not conflate canary rollouts and A/B unless hypothesis explicitly targets quality/UX.
- Use cohort orthogonalization to avoid overlap with other experiments (steward must check the experiment registry).
- Pre-register primary/secondary metrics and minimum detectable effect (MDE) in the exposure note.

Lightweight comms templates (for steward to use):
- Activation note subject: "[Activation] <feature> - waves + timebox - steward: <name>"
- Body (short): summary, waves, primary signals, rollback link, expected performance impact, stakeholders. Paste dashboards and links.

Simulation and smoke plan (cheap checks before Wave 0):
- Run synthetic load that simulates 3x peak token rate for 15m to validate autoscaler behavior.
- Run A/B offline simulation using last 72h logs to simulate model quality delta and verify the MDE assumptions. (owner: ML)

Open questions / TODOs (action items):
- [ ] Define a small canonical eval set for activation checks (owner: ML) — we need a < 500 sample quick-run set that maps to product-critical queries.
- [ ] Automate the "activation note" template as a PR generator for the release repo (owner: release-eng).
- [ ] Add a dedicated visibility toggle in Console to mark "stewarded activation" traffic slices (owner: console team).
- [ ] Decide if the steward role should rotate per quarter or per release stream (proposal: rotate per release stream).

Edge cases and friction points we anticipate:
- Multi-customer config: partial rollbacks are messy if different cohorts have pinned features — need per-customer unexposed toggle in Console.
- Long-tail regression detection: many problems show up > 12h; recommend a secondary "stability watch" for 48h after full roll.

Notes to self / meeting scraps:
- Keep ceremony < 30m for routine activations. Heavy-weight reviews only for high-risk or cross-org features.
- For low-risk UX-only changes, steward can fast-pass with one SRE + one ML sign-off and a 1h watch.

References and scratch links:
- Confluence: experiment-framework-v2 (see linked_artifacts)
- GH: rollout-sim/chefbook-proto branch (proto scripts for slice simulation)
- Linear: EXP-204 tracks the steward pilot for Q4 2025

If you're reading this and want to pilot the chefbook flow: reply here with the feature name + tentative date. Will pair with SRE to run the simulation and finalize wave sizes.

-- Priya
(sprint notes; not final; synthesize into short playbook when we validate two activations)
